observations.status: Partial primary-text assessment, not accepted record evidence
observations.finding: Three source-labelled residue powders, SAR-Ni 30167, SAR-In 32083 and SAR-Re 30168, came from nickel/cobalt-based superalloy bars supplied by AAS Ltd., Sheffield. Introduction discusses production/cutting dust and Results states different manufacturing origins. Exact alloy designations and individual process provenance remain unresolved. These stock labels must not be treated as elemental identifiers or mineral species.

observations.status: Methods text inspected; figures not inspected
observations.finding: Approximately 35 g of each heterogeneous feed was milled with eight 20 mm stainless-steel balls at 300 rpm for 10 min; the below-250 µm fraction was retained. Aqua-regia analysis used 10 mL acid, 5% w/v solid, four-hour reflux, 0.2 µm filtration and ICP-OES, with mean ± SEM and n=3.

observations.status: Methods text inspected; no strain mapping accepted
observations.finding: A. thiooxidans and an unresolved sulfur/iron-oxidizing consortium were obtained from Bangor University Acidophile Culture Collection. The culture-produced lixiviants were filtered at 0.2 µm before contacting residue: this is cell-free spent-medium treatment, not demonstrated microbial growth on alloy. Stock accessions and consortium membership remain unresolved.

The culture medium was initially acidified to pH 1.8 with sulfuric acid. Bio-acid treatment began at pH 1.0, Bio-ferric at pH 1.8 with 45 mM ferric iron, and combined treatment at pH 1.0 with 45 mM ferric iron. One percent w/v solid in 100 mL was incubated at 30 °C, 130 rpm for seven days. Unequal starting acidity prevents reading the treatment contrast as an isolated acid-versus-ferric mechanism comparison. A matched chemical-acid/ferric blank is not established by the sections inspected; this is not a claim that none exists elsewhere.

Yield is liquid metal concentration times solution volume divided by feed mass times measured feed metal concentration. The feed concentrations derive from aqua-regia digestion, while §3.1 explicitly acknowledges partial digestion and residual base metals. A future record must distinguish this operational denominator from demonstrated whole-feed inventory or isolated-product recovery.

The parsed table gives SAR-Re 30168 cobalt as 65.30 g/kg, whereas the later discussion says a 10% improvement corresponds to about 7.45 g/kg Co. Read the original table, graph and denominator before choosing or converting either value.

Agitation treatments are 130, 200 and 270 rpm; peroxide series adds 1–7 mL of 30% H2O2 to 100 mL bio-acid, described as 100–700 mM, at 270 rpm and 30 °C for ten days. Verify dose and final-volume conventions and all plotted controls. Higher early-stage mobilization must not obscure later lower-speed counterevidence or the weaker SAR-In response.

observations.section: Data Availability; Funding; Conflicts of Interest
observations.finding: The paper says contributions are included in the article and inquiries may be directed to the authors. It reports joint Advanced Alloy Services/Coventry funding and that author Stephen Hall works for the company supplying material. No complete raw-data or supplementary-file inventory was established. Laboratory flask observations would not demonstrate industrial biological deployment, life-cycle benefit, absence of emissions, or cost advantage.
